classification.difficultyReason: The parts supply the whole route: the two conditions (k>0 and Δ<0), then Δ, then the inequality, then the combination. The student computes Δ=4-4k² with a=c=k, factorises and solves 4-4k²<0 with no graph supplied, so must picture the downward parabola in k to get the outside region. They then intersect k<-1 or k>1 with k>0. The only change of representation is moving between conditions on the parabola and inequalities in k, which is routine and linked. This is harder than the single-idea explanation in p68-q11 and a little easier than p67-q8, which asks for open-ended interpretation of two representations.

classification.difficultyReason: The task is only to move all terms to one side and factorise 3x²-5x-2 into (3x+1)(x-2). There is no solving or interpreting of the inequality. The factorisation has a non-monic leading coefficient, which needs a short search for the right split of the middle term. That makes it more than direct application of a single rule like A1. There are no hidden decisions or representation changes, and it is easier than p64-q1, which asks for a graph reading of a solution set.
